question: Does shared history geometry support reference-calibrated evidence decoding across unseen parameter seeds and held-out histories?
histories: All 64 lexicographically ordered binary six-cue histories. Held-out means unseen by the fitted readout, not a previously unmeasured binary string.
split_rule: Permute 32 complementary history pairs (i,63-i), i=0..31. First 8 pairs are 16 anchors; next 12 pairs are 24 fit histories; remaining 12 pairs are 24 evaluation histories. All sets disjoint, fixed across seeds and delays.
anchor_features: 16 Euclidean distances to anchor states, divided by RMS centered anchor norm. Corresponding anchors are collected per seed and time; no evaluation labels enter calibration. Separate ridge readout per delay, alpha=1, fitted only on fit histories in four train seeds. Train-only feature standardization with intercept.
precision_rule: If RMS anchor scatter <= 10*float32_eps*max(1,RMS anchor norm), mark precision-limited and use zero features. Such cells cannot support a positive gate; failure does not establish erasure. Geometry and residual geometry require centered RMS signal above the same floor based on ORIGINAL state norm, not residual norm; unavailable values are null.
controls: anchor-centered/scaled raw QR16 projection with same train boundary
train labels shuffled within final-symbol strata, shared across fitting seeds
frozen decoder evaluated under 32 fixed anchor permutations, report 95th percentile R2
analytic latest-cue log odds (zero here because final reliability .5)
separately fitted within-seed anchor probe diagnostic
anchor-fitted affine signed-six-bit state model followed by the same distance-feature pipeline
frozen tanh reservoir with 1312 state coordinates, spectral radius .9, leak1, fixed random input projection
baseline_match: Same public frames, number of histories, seeds, delays, state width for reservoir, split and probe rules. Parameter count, input mixing and dynamical regime differ; no architecture superiority criterion.
geometry: centered effective rank and PC1 fraction
train-history linear signed-bit model evaluated on held-out histories
cross-seed RDM comparison after train-fitted signed-bit residualization
decision_rule: Per primary delay, anchor R2 >= .10 and >= .10 above latest, conditional-label shuffle and the 95th percentile permuted-anchor R2 in at least 5 of 6 evaluation seeds, with precision-valid features. Overall passes only if all four delays pass. Report linear-response, raw and within-seed controls separately. No retuning.
falsifier: Anchor-based transfer does not meet the frozen gate despite high cross-seed distance agreement. Separately, adequacy of the affine surrogate undermines an interpretation requiring nonlinear computation; it does not negate a positive transfer gate.
inference_unit: Evaluation parameter seed. Histories, seed pairs, delays and controls are dependent; no pairwise-count significance claims.
claim_boundary: Reference-calibrated external transfer and descriptive geometry; no autonomous readout, causal channel, adaptation, architecture advantage or common aligned coordinates.
